comparator.name: Public Administration (Bestuurskunde)
comparator.sourceNotes: The official 2026–27 curriculum accounts for exactly 180 ECTS: 60 compulsory ECTS in year 1, 60 compulsory ECTS in year 2, and year 3 with 42 compulsory ECTS plus an 18-ECTS mobility window or minor. Zero-credit orientation, Dutch-language testing and GROW development are excluded from the total. The 12-ECTS year-long public-administration placement, 12-ECTS thesis and genuine 18-ECTS minor or exchange space remain explicit; no elective content is invented.
components: Inleiding Organisatiewetgeving voor de Publieke Sector
Genuine 18-ECTS open minor or mobility space; no specific elective content is invented.

core: Public administration, government and the organisation of public institutions
Public policy formation, implementation and evaluation of societal problems
Politics, democratic governance and political decision-making
Constitutional and administrative law, rule of law and accountability
Public organisations, management and collaboration with civil society
Public finance and empirical public-administration research
adjacent: Local and regional governance and cross-sector cooperation
European governance and comparative public institutions
questions: How can governments design and evaluate responses to complex social problems?
How can public authority remain democratic, lawful and accountable?
How can public organisations collaborate and manage competing interests effectively?

alternatives.label: Public governance, policy & institutions
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum balances public policy, politics, law, sociology, economics, organisations, research and accountability around the operation of government.
alternatives.concept: A broad closest feasible Public Administration programme combining government and policy, democratic institutions, law, sociology, economics, organisational management, communication and research.
progression: Foundations in politics, sociology, economics, law and research precede advanced policy, public management, constitutional and European law, leadership, social theory, accountability and independent research. Formal prerequisites and verified offerings are respected; seven level-3 courses provide advanced depth.

alternatives.label: Public organisations, management & collaboration
alternatives.labelReason: The completed programme centres organisational behaviour, leadership, management, communication and cross-sector cooperation while retaining policy, law and economics.
alternatives.concept: A public-organisations pathway focused on management, leadership, organisational behaviour, communication and collaboration among government, civil society and market actors, supported by politics, economics and research.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, eleven courses shift emphasis from broad public law, political institutions and policy analysis toward business foundations, organisational behaviour, leadership, communication, strategy and management research.
progression: Foundations in politics, economics, organisations, sociology and research precede advanced leadership, strategy, communication, public economics, social theory and organisational research. All formal prerequisites and verified offerings are respected; seven level-3 courses provide advanced depth.

alternatives.label: Law, democracy & European governance
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum gives sustained weight to constitutional, administrative, European and international law alongside democratic institutions, history, politics and policy.
alternatives.concept: A public-law and European-governance pathway combining constitutional and international law, politics, democratic institutions, European history, economics, sociology, research and public accountability.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, eight courses replace leadership, public-management and applied-policy content with additional law, European history, political institutions, social movements and transnational organisational perspectives. It differs from the organisational pathway in thirteen courses.
progression: Introductory politics, history, sociology, economics and research precede constitutional, European and international law, advanced politics, institutional history and independent research. Formal prerequisites and verified offerings are respected; seven level-3 courses provide advanced depth.

selection.assessment: The closest match owns the broad public-administration, policy, politics, democratic-governance, accountability and societal-problem core. The public-organisations cluster and the public-law and European-governance cluster each have direct programme-interest support, coherent feasible schedules and pairwise differences above 30 ECTS. Three alternatives is the maximum, and every generator-eligible row is owned exactly once.

notes.text: Tilburg combines public administration, law, politics, sociology, economics and organisations in a fixed two-year sequence, then requires a 12-ECTS public-sector placement and 12-ECTS thesis. UCR can build coherent governance, public-organisation and public-law pathways, but it does not reproduce the compulsory professional placement or the same integrated disciplinary spine; the 18-ECTS mobility window is preserved as genuine open space.
The Tilburg programme is Dutch-taught, whereas UCR is English-taught. This comparison assesses academic content and structure rather than language of instruction.
